task: Fix two bug reports from the user: (1) the runtime judge in sandbox.worker.ts rejects solutions whose return values contain `undefined` even though safeOut (display) renders those positions as `null` — e.g. `Promise.allSettled` solutions that resolve to `[null, 4, null]` via `d.value` produce `[undefined, 4, undefined]` and are marked failing; (2) the Submit button never asks for confirmation, so a user can submit a run whose cases haven't all passed without a deliberate `submit anyway` step.

analysis.objective: Fix two bugs in the leetlab judge/editor flow: (1) the worker deep-equality check rejects solutions whose return value contains `undefined` even though `JSON.stringify` (the displayed output) renders those positions as `null`, so e.g. `Promise.allSettled`-style solutions that resolve to `[null, 4, null]` via `d.value` produce `[undefined, 4, undefined]` and are marked failing; (2) the Submit button never asks for confirmation, so a user can submit a run whose cases have not all passed without a deliberate `submit anyway` step.
analysis.successDefinition: Solutions whose values JSON-normalize to the expected text (e.g. `[null,4,null]`) now pass the worker deep-equality check instead of being incorrectly failed; the Submit button, when clicked after a run whose verdict is anything other than `Accepted`, opens a confirmation dialog that names the pass count (`Passed X / Y`) and lets the user choose `Cancel` or `Submit anyway`; on `Accepted` the dialog is skipped and submission proceeds as today; existing passing cases continue to pass; `tsc -b && vite build` and `vitest run` stay green.
assumptions: Scope is exactly the two named bugs and their tests — not a broader rewrite of the judge or the Submit flow.
Quality bar stays `prototype` (matches the horizon-1 vision and the project's existing test coverage).

`undefined` vs `null` mismatch is the only reported comparison bug; the JSON-displayed-vs-compared gap is the minimal fix target. NaN, BigInt, and key-ordering edge cases are out of scope unless a test actually fails after the fix.
The confirmation dialog should fire only when `verdict !== 'Accepted'`; passing runs submit directly without a prompt (matches the user's wording: 'submit problematic cases').
The dialog is short and lives inline in `EditorPane.tsx` — no need for a generic modal primitive or portal infrastructure for one screen.
No new dependencies; no API contract changes for the store.
Class-mode already normalizes `undefined -> null` at line 356 of `sandbox.worker.ts`; the fn-mode comparison is the actual gap. The fix only needs to cover `runFn`.
Existing direct deepEq semantics are intentional for cases where the answer is a plain primitive (e.g. `4` vs `null` should still fail).

risks.name: Over-broad normalization breaks legitimate failures
risks.detail: Treating `undefined === null` globally could make `return undefined` accidentally pass a problem that expected `null`. Mitigation: normalize only on the comparison side (preserve the original `out` for the displayed `output` field), and limit the rule to array members / object values where JSON does the same collapse — not bare top-level returns.

risks.name: Submission UX regression — silent failure when verdict is failing
risks.detail: If the confirmation dialog errors out, a user would lose the ability to submit a non-Accepted run entirely. Mitigation: the Submit button still calls handleRun(true) on confirm; the dialog is a guard, not a gate.

risks.name: NaN handling regression
risks.detail: Current deepEq has explicit NaN handling; a naive switch to JSON comparison would drop it. Mitigation: keep deepEq as the inner comparator and add a pre-normalization step that converts `undefined` to `null` recursively in array slots and object values before deepEq runs.

risks.name: Marker state leaks across problems
risks.detail: The confirmation dialog must read the `verdict` from the *current* problem's last run, not module state. Reuse `useAppStore.getState().lastRuns[currentSlug]` rather than a local variable.

outOfScope: Rewriting the judge to a richer expectation grammar (e.g. matcher-by-matcher, custom comparator per problem, snapshot tests).
Persisting submissions to a server; current localStorage-based `addSubmission` is unchanged.
Adding a generic modal/portal primitive or refactoring existing modals (GenerateModal, ImportModal, Drawer) — the new dialog stays local in EditorPane.
Surfacing the verdict table in a deeper result panel; existing verdict pills/marks are untouched.
Re-running the fold or autocomplete work from horizon 1; no Discovery entry on those topics mentions any regression.
Coverage of every rejection-shape corner case (objects with undefined keys, sparse arrays as roots, Promise object identity) — only the demonstrated case (fn-return undefined-in-array) needs to pass.

ubiquitousLanguage.definition: the sandbox web worker + comparison logic that runs a problem's test cases against user code
one element of `Problem.tests` — a single input/expected pair (or call/expected for class mode)
the top-level status of a run: 'Accepted' (all passed), 'Wrong Answer' / 'No Expected Cases' / 'Time Limit Exceeded' / 'Compile Error'
the worker-side recursive equality function used to grade each case
the `JSON.stringify`-based wrapper used to render user outputs into the result panel
a small inline modal that asks the user to confirm `Submit` when the last run's verdict is not `Accepted`

analysis.domainShapeReason: Both changes are local to the worker judge comparison (`sandbox.worker.ts`) and the editor submit handler (`EditorPane.tsx`); no business entities, rules, or workflows are introduced. This continues the technical shape established in horizon 1's vision.

discoveryFindings.finding: Single runtime equality helper `deepEq` in `src/infrastructure/sandbox.worker.ts` lines 28-55; called from `runFn` at line 269 (`pass = hasExp ? deepEq(out, c.expected) : null`) and from `runClass` at line 386.
discoveryFindings.implication: A single normalization step added before `deepEq` in `runFn` fixes the user's undefined-vs-null case without touching class-mode (which already normalizes undefined -> null at line 356).

discoveryFindings.finding: No stringify-based fallback exists in the worker; `JSON.stringify` is used only inside `safeOut` (line 22) for diagnostic rendering, not for equality.
discoveryFindings.implication: Discrepancy between displayed output (`safeOut` shows undefined as `null` in arrays) and graded equality (`deepEq` returns false) is real and reproducible.

discoveryFindings.finding: `src/infrastructure/sandboxAmbient.test.ts` fixture-driven tests for the ambient `.d.ts` host; representative names: `declares exactly the aggregator handles, typed, in global scope`, `serves the full transitive import closure of the aggregator`.
discoveryFindings.implication: New judge tests should follow the same fixture style for file-level assertions.

discoveryFindings.finding: `src/infrastructure/sandboxE2E.test.ts` loads `sandbox.worker.ts` directly, captures `postMessage`, invokes `self.onmessage` with a synthetic `MessageEvent`. Representative: `runs to completion, exercising redis, pg, rabbitmq, kafka, queue`, `emits a trace line for every service call in the {l,t} case-log stream`.
discoveryFindings.implication: The user can run real worker code in tests without spinning up a browser worker — the precedent for adding `deepEq(undefined-vs-null)` cases to a worker test file.

discoveryFindings.finding: No test file covers `src/components/EditorPane.tsx`. Grep for `EditorPane`, `btn-submit`, or `"Submit"` returns zero hits across `src/**.test.*`.
discoveryFindings.implication: Submit UI has zero coverage today. A new EditorPane.test.ts is appropriate; @testing-library/react is not currently a devDep (need to verify before adding).

discoveryFindings.finding: Submit button at `src/components/EditorPane.tsx` lines 312-319 calls `onClick={() => handleRun(true)}`. No existing confirmation/modal exists inside EditorPane.
discoveryFindings.implication: Confirmation dialog must be added from scratch; not rewriting an existing control.

discoveryFindings.finding: `src/components/ManageProvidersModal.tsx` line 89 uses local state `const [confirmingId, setConfirmingId] = useState<string | null>(null)` and a two-stage inline button for delete confirmation, rather than a nested modal.
discoveryFindings.implication: The close precedent for a small inline confirmation is `ManageProvidersModal`, not the full `ImportModal` shell. Mirror that pattern.

discoveryFindings.finding: EditorPane only WRITES to `lastRuns` (via `setLastRun(currentSlug, lastRun)` at line 154) and constructs `verdict` strings at lines 137/192/222. It does NOT read `verdict` back. Drawer.tsx:16 reads via selector. DescPane reads submission-history verdicts, not run-time last-verdict.
discoveryFindings.implication: Three options for the confirmation source: (a) new derived selector, (b) imperative `useAppStore.getState().lastRuns?.[currentSlug]?.verdict` inside the handler, or (c) reuse the local `verdict` variable computed in `handleRun` itself — option (c) is the lowest-blast-radius choice because no extra reads or selectors are required.

discoveryFindings.finding: `handleRun(isSubmit)` already computes `let verdict = 'Wrong Answer'` then conditionally overwrites with `'Accepted'`/`'No Expected Cases'`/`'Time Limit Exceeded'`/`'Compile Error'` and uses the value both for the `addSubmission` payload and as part of `lastRun`.
discoveryFindings.implication: The Submit click handler can read the most recent `verdict` from the last `handleRun` call by reading `lastRuns[currentSlug].verdict`, but a simpler alternative is to expose `verdict` as a small piece of component state set at the end of handleRun. Either avoids re-running the worker.

discoveryFindings.finding: No test in the repo compares arrays/objects where `undefined` and `null` appear in equivalent positions. The only deepEq-relevant trace assertions in `sandboxE2E.test.ts` (lines 192-200) check literal `'-> undefined'` strings in `safeOut` traces — these are display-only and unaffected by a deepEq change.
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding a new test for `[undefined, 4, undefined]` vs `[null, 4, null]` via the worker runner has no existing test that would now fail spuriously.

phases.name: Make the runner treat undefined positions as null
phases.rationale: When user code returns an array containing `undefined` (typical with `Promise.allSettled`, where `d.value` is `undefined` for rejected promises), the worker `deepEq` rejects it as not equal to the expected `null`, even though `safeOut` — the same module's output-rendering helper — renders both as `null` via `JSON.stringify`. Result: solutions the user can plainly see match the expected output are still graded wrong. The class-mode path already normalizes method-return `undefined` to `null` (line 356), so this only needs to land for `runFn`. The fix is narrow and self-contained: a normalization step between raw user output and the existing comparison.
changes: Add a small `normalizeUndefinedForJson` helper near `deepEq` (around line 56 of sandbox.worker.ts) that recursively walks arrays and plain objects and converts each `undefined` slot/key value to `null`, matching `JSON.stringify`'s behavior. Top-level primitives and class instance values pass through untouched.

In `runFn` (line 269), apply the helper to `out` only — not to `c.expected` — just before `deepEq(out, c.expected)`: `const pass = hasExp ? deepEq(normalizeUndefinedForJson(out), c.expected) : null`. Leave the `safeOut(out)` call below it untouched so the displayed `output` field still shows the literal `undefined` (preserving the existing diagnostic shape for unbroken cases).
Do not touch `runClass` — line 356 already normalizes `undefined -> null` for method returns, and `c.expected` is the trusted author-supplied reference, so no recursive walk is needed there.

Add a new test file `src/infrastructure/sandboxDeepEq.test.ts` modeled on `sandboxE2E.test.ts`'s onmessage-capture pattern (loads `sandbox.worker.ts`, posts a synthetic RunMsg, inspects the `case` messages). Cover at minimum: (a) user code returning `[undefined, 4, undefined]` against `expected = [null, 4, null]` produces `pass: true`; (b) user code returning `4` against `expected = null` still produces `pass: false`; (c) a NaN case (e.g. `expected = [NaN]` vs `out = [NaN]`) still passes (deepEq NaN handling is preserved).
phases.goal: Stop the runner from failing solutions whose values JSON-normalize to the expected.
phases.expectedResult: `src/infrastructure/sandboxDeepEq.test.ts` exists; `npm test` is green; existing test suite (`vitest run`) passes unchanged; `tsc -b` and `vite build` stay green; at least one worker-driven test exercises `out = [undefined, 4, undefined]` against `expected = [null, 4, null]` and reports `pass: true`.

rubric.label: Normalization matches JSON.stringify shape
rubric.ruleStatement: The new helper recursively walks arrays and plain-object value slots and replaces `undefined` with `null` only there, matching `JSON.stringify` exactly. It is applied only to `out` (not to `c.expected`) immediately before the `deepEq` call inside `runFn`, and the value rendered by `safeOut` for the diagnostic `output` line is the pre-normalization literal.
rubric.passCriteria: A worker-driven test posts a RunMsg whose fn returns `[undefined, 4, undefined]` against `expected = [null, 4, null]` and the captured case message reports `pass: true`. The same case's trace line still contains the literal `-> undefined` (or equivalent `safeOut` rendering), proving display was not normalized. Expected values are never passed through the helper.
failureExamples: Helper recurses into array elements but skips object value slots, so `{ a: undefined }` vs `{ a: null }` still fails even though both JSON-stringify to `{"a":null}`.
Helper normalizes both `out` and `c.expected`, masking author-side typos in expected fixtures and breaking the asymmetry between trusted and untrusted inputs.
Helper mutates `out` in place (e.g., `arr[i] = null`) instead of producing a new value, contaminating the second case of a problem whose input state lingers.

rubric.label: Blast radius limited to runFn
rubric.ruleStatement: Only the `runFn` pass comparison is touched. `runClass` keeps its existing `undefined -> null` coercion at line 356 untouched. `safeOut` is not modified, so trace diagnostics and the result panel keep rendering the literal `undefined` token. No other call site of `deepEq` is re-routed through the new helper.
rubric.passCriteria: `sandboxE2E.test.ts`'s existing assertions about `safeOut` trace lines containing `-> undefined` still pass unchanged. A class-mode run whose method returns `undefined` against `expected = null` still passes through the existing line-356 path, not through the new helper. No additional export is introduced beyond the helper itself, and the helper is referenced exactly once.
failureExamples: Helper is applied at both the `runFn` site and the `runClass` deepEq site, double-normalizing class-mode method returns and creating drift between fn-mode and class-mode display.
Helper is also passed into `safeOut(out)` to 'keep things consistent', which silently rewrites the displayed `output` field to `null` and breaks every trace assertion that grepped for `-> undefined`.
Helper is exported and re-used by another future feature in the same PR, expanding the change beyond the phase's stated scope.

rubric.label: Edge cases preserved (primitives, NaN, sparse, instances)
rubric.ruleStatement: Top-level primitive returns (e.g., `4` vs `null`) still fail the comparison. deepEq's `NaN === NaN` semantics are preserved. Sparse-array holes are not invented as `null`. Class-instance and other non-plain-object values pass through the helper untouched. A bare `return undefined` against `expected = null` does not start passing just because the helper exists.
rubric.passCriteria: Worker-driven test asserts `pass: false` for `out = 4` vs `expected = null`; asserts `pass: true` for `out = [NaN]` vs `expected = [NaN]`; asserts that a sparse root like `[1, ,3]` is not silently filled with `null`. The helper's recursion guards on `Array.isArray` and a plain-object prototype check, and ignores anything else.
failureExamples: Helper normalizes the root value too, so `return undefined` against `expected = null` starts passing when the original semantics should mark it as a wrong answer.

Helper is implemented via `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(out))`, which converts `NaN` to `null`, drops `undefined` array holes, and silently rewrites sparse roots — all three regressions land in one move.

Helper recurses into class instances and converts `instance.foo === undefined` slots into `null`, so a class-mode method that intentionally returns `undefined` for an unset field gets graded as `null` against an expected `undefined`.

rubric.label: Worker-driven test exercises the real pipeline
rubric.ruleStatement: The new `sandboxDeepEq.test.ts` loads `sandbox.worker.ts` directly and posts a synthetic RunMsg via the `self.onmessage` capture pattern used by `sandboxE2E.test.ts`, rather than importing `deepEq` or the helper in isolation. The test covers both the kept-passing case and at least two kept-failing cases so a wiring regression that flips a primitive wrong-answer into pass:true is caught.
rubric.passCriteria: At least three assertions live in the same worker-driven test: (a) `out = [undefined, 4, undefined]` vs `expected = [null, 4, null]` returns `pass: true`; (b) `out = 4` vs `expected = null` returns `pass: false`; (c) `out = [NaN]` vs `expected = [NaN]` returns `pass: true`. The captured messages come from `postMessage`/case events, not from a unit test of the helper.
failureExamples: Test imports `deepEq` and the helper directly and only asserts the helper's return value, so a wiring mistake in `runFn` (helper applied to the wrong argument or not at all) goes undetected.
Test covers case (a) but omits cases (b) and (c), so a regression that flips `4 vs null` to passing silently passes the new test.
Test stubs `self.onmessage` and bypasses `postMessage`, so a future refactor that renames the worker message format breaks in production but not in CI.

rubric.label: No regression in existing suite or build
rubric.ruleStatement: `npm test` (vitest run) is fully green including the pre-existing `sandboxE2E.test.ts`, `sandboxAmbient.test.ts`, and any other infrastructure test. `tsc -b` and `vite build` stay green. No existing assertion is weakened, deleted, or skipped to make the suite pass.
rubric.passCriteria: `vitest run` reports all pre-existing tests passing without modification; `tsc -b && vite build` exits 0; no test file has a `.skip`, `.todo`, or a relaxed comparison added in this phase.
failureExamples: `sandboxE2E.test.ts` assertion that greps trace lines for `-> undefined` starts failing because the helper was also wired into `safeOut`; the developer then deletes the assertion instead of fixing the wiring.
An existing test that asserts `pass: false` for a primitive wrong-answer case is softened to `pass: undefined` or `toBeLessThanOrEqual` to silence it after the helper over-normalizes.
`tsc -b` fails because the helper signature is loose (e.g., `any`) and the developer adds `// @ts-ignore` instead of typing the recursion properly.

phases.healerHint: Re-read sandbox.worker.ts: safeOut (~line 22), the runFn pass comparison (~line 269), the runClass undefined-to-null coercion (~line 356), and the runClass deepEq call (~line 386). Wire the new helper into exactly one place — between `out` and `deepEq(out, c.expected)` inside runFn — and never pass the normalized value into safeOut or into c.expected. Restrict recursion to Array.isArray and a plain-object prototype check so top-level primitives, NaN, sparse holes, and class instances all pass through. If a `[undefined,4,undefined] vs [null,4,null]` test still fails, the helper is missing or applied to the wrong side; if a `4 vs null` test now incorrectly passes, the helper is over-normalizing the root; if a `[NaN] vs [NaN]` test regresses, the helper is using JSON round-trip — switch to explicit recursion that preserves holes and NaN. Verify by running `npm test` plus `tsc -b && vite build`.

phases.name: Ask before submitting a run that failed cases
phases.rationale: Today the Submit button in `EditorPane.tsx` always calls `handleRun(true)` directly. When the most-recent run's verdict is anything other than `Accepted` — `Wrong Answer`, `Time Limit Exceeded`, `Compile Error`, `No Expected Cases` — the submission lands silently with no deliberate `submit anyway` step. The user has explicitly asked for a confirmation prompt so a non-passing submission is a chosen action, not a mis-click. This is also a natural safety net for the case where Phase 1's normalization is not yet in or has regressed: even if the test report is wrong, the user can decide whether to submit anyway. The pattern is small enough to live inline — no modal portal needed.
changes: Add local component state `const [pendingSubmit, setPendingSubmit] = useState(false)` next to the existing `busy` / `fmtBusy` hooks.

Change the Submit `onClick` (around line 314) so it first reads the current verdict: `const last = useAppStore.getState().lastRuns?.[currentSlug]`. If `last` is null/undefined OR `last.verdict === 'Accepted'`, call `handleRun(true)` immediately as today. Otherwise call `setPendingSubmit(true)` and stop.

Render a small inline confirmation block immediately under the editor-foot toolbar when `pendingSubmit` is true. The block shows the last-run pass/total counts (`Passed {last.passed} / {last.total}` — falls back to `0 / 0` when not yet available) plus two buttons: `Cancel` (clears `pendingSubmit`, no submit) and `Submit anyway` (calls `handleRun(true)` then clears `pendingSubmit`). Mirror the small inline-confirmation pattern from `src/components/ManageProvidersModal.tsx:89` (local useState + a two-stage block, no modal portal, no overlay).

Clear `pendingSubmit` when `currentSlug` changes (a useEffect on `currentSlug`), and clear it whenever a successful new run starts (`busy` flipping back to `false` after a run that has just set a fresh verdict) — use the existing `lastRun.verdict` change as the trigger.

If `EditorPane.test.ts` does not exist and `@testing-library/react` is not in `package.json`, do NOT introduce it for this horizon — keep blast radius small. Add at minimum a manual smoke-test note in the phase report: clicking Submit after a Wrong-Answer run opens the block; clicking Submit Anyway invokes `handleRun(true)`; clicking Cancel closes without submitting; switching problems clears the state; an Accepted run never opens the block.

If the package.json check reveals a DOM test is already in place for EditorPane (it does not today), add at minimum one test covering the predicate path: clicking Submit with verdict `Wrong Answer` opens the block with pass/total counts visible.
phases.goal: Make Submit on a failing run a deliberate choice.
phases.expectedResult: After this phase, clicking Submit with `lastRuns[currentSlug]?.verdict === 'Wrong Answer' | 'Time Limit Exceeded' | 'Compile Error' | 'No Expected Cases'` opens an inline confirmation block listing the last-run pass/total counts and two buttons (`Cancel`, `Submit anyway`); clicking `Cancel` closes the block without invoking `handleRun(true)`; clicking `Submit anyway` invokes `handleRun(true)` and closes the block; clicking Submit with `verdict === 'Accepted'` OR no `lastRun` proceeds directly to `handleRun(true)` (no block); the block clears when the problem changes; `tsc -b && vite build` stay green.

rubric.label: Submit-click branch logic
rubric.ruleStatement: Guard against the Submit button doing the wrong thing on each verdict shape — the three-way branch (Accepted → direct submit, non-Accepted → block, no lastRun → safe default) must be exhaustive and read from the current problem's last run at click time, not from a stale closure or a captured handleRun variable.
rubric.passCriteria: Clicking Submit when lastRuns[currentSlug]?.verdict === 'Accepted' calls handleRun(true) with no block ever rendered; clicking Submit for any of {Wrong Answer, Time Limit Exceeded, Compile Error, No Expected Cases} sets pendingSubmit=true and renders the block; clicking Submit before any run lands in the documented safe default (either opens the block with 0 / 0 or submits directly, but the choice is explicit and consistent); the verdict is read via useAppStore.getState().lastRuns?.[currentSlug]?.verdict inside the onClick, so a problem switch that changes the verdict before the click uses the fresh value.
failureExamples: Reads last.verdict from a local component variable captured during the previous handleRun call, so the block opens (or fails to open) using the previous problem's verdict after switching problems
Special-cases only 'Wrong Answer' and lets 'Compile Error' and 'Time Limit Exceeded' slip through to a direct submit, missing the user's explicit 'submit problematic cases' requirement
Treats null lastRuns[currentSlug] as 'no confirmation needed' and submits directly without flagging that the choice was made implicitly
Uses a useAppStore selector subscription whose closure was captured at mount time, so a problem switch updates the store but the branch decision still uses the old slug

rubric.label: Confirmation block content and button wiring
rubric.ruleStatement: Guard against the block being a half-built shell — the user must see why they're being asked to confirm, and both buttons must do exactly what their labels say, with no implicit state.
rubric.passCriteria: The block visibly renders the last-run pass/total in the form 'Passed {last.passed} / {last.total}' (falling back to '0 / 0' only if last is unavailable at render time); Cancel calls setPendingSubmit(false) only and never invokes handleRun; Submit anyway invokes handleRun(true) and then clears pendingSubmit in the same tick; both are real <button type="button"> elements (not <div onClick>) so they are keyboard-reachable; clicking Submit anyway while busy is either disabled or guarded so it cannot double-submit; the block is rendered as a sibling of the editor-foot toolbar, not inside a portal.
failureExamples: Renders the two buttons but forgets the 'Passed X / Y' count, so the user has no context for whether to confirm a near-pass run
Wires Cancel to handleRun(true) by accident (typo or copy-paste from Submit anyway), inverting the confirmation semantics
Calls handleRun(true) on Submit anyway but forgets to clear pendingSubmit afterward, leaving the block mounted and re-firing the submit on subsequent clicks
Uses <div onClick={...}> for the buttons to 'match the inline look', breaking keyboard activation and screen-reader affordance

rubric.label: Block state lifecycle (no leaks across problems or runs)
rubric.ruleStatement: Guard against the block's open/closed state leaking across problems or surviving the run that should have resolved it.
rubric.passCriteria: When currentSlug changes, pendingSubmit is reset to false on the next render (via a useEffect on currentSlug or the React-during-render reset pattern used in ManageProvidersModal); when a new run completes (busy transitions false→true→false), the block is closed regardless of whether the run returned Accepted, Wrong Answer, Compile Error, TLE, or threw; switching problems mid-confirmation never triggers an accidental submit; the block is not visible on the new problem's first render even if the previous problem left it open.
failureExamples: Resets pendingSubmit only when Cancel or Submit anyway is clicked, so a problem switch leaves the stale block mounted over the new problem's editor
Clears pendingSubmit in handleRun's happy path but not in the Compile Error early-return or the TLE catch branch, so failed runs leave the block open after the next run lands
Adds currentSlug to the component but forgets it in the useEffect dependency array, so the reset never fires under React strict mode

Tries to clear pendingSubmit inside handleRun after setLastRun, but handleRun is also called from the Submit anyway button — the block closes only when the user is the one who opened it, not when a stale open state happens to coincide

rubric.label: Style consistency with the inline-confirm precedent
rubric.ruleStatement: Guard against introducing a new modal/portal primitive or visual language for one screen — the block must mirror the inline-confirm pattern in ManageProvidersModal.tsx:89 (local useState + two-stage block, no portal, no overlay, no new component file).
rubric.passCriteria: The block lives inline in EditorPane's JSX (no createPortal, no overlay div, no new <Modal> or <ConfirmDialog> component); uses local useState for the open/closed state; reuses existing button classNames already present in the editor-foot stylesheet (or, if a new class is required, it is a single class added to the existing stylesheet, not a new theme primitive); no new CSS file is introduced; no React portal imports are added to EditorPane; the block visually sits in the same row rhythm as the existing Run Code / Submit buttons.
failureExamples: Reaches for createPortal + a new .modal-overlay div because ManageProvidersModal uses createPortal elsewhere, missing that ManageProvidersModal's line-89 confirmation itself is a plain inline block
Extracts a generic ConfirmDialog component file to 'reuse later' when only one call site exists today (YAGNI violation, blast radius creep)
Adds a new confirm-block.css file with bespoke typography instead of reusing the editor-foot button classes that already style adjacent actions
Imports createPortal from react-dom at the top of EditorPane.tsx for a block that does not need to escape its parent's overflow

rubric.label: Build and test pipeline stays green, no scope creep
rubric.ruleStatement: Guard against the phase breaking the build pipeline or smuggling in a new test-library dependency that isn't justified by existing test infrastructure.
rubric.passCriteria: `tsc -b` passes; `vite build` passes; `vitest run` stays green with no pre-existing test file modified or skipped; no new runtime dependency is added; @testing-library/react is NOT added to package.json unless it is already a devDep at the start of the phase (and even then, only if a DOM test is being added); if no DOM test framework is currently in place, the phase adds a manual smoke-test note in the phase report rather than introducing one; no shared type in infrastructure/store.ts is edited (the verdict read path is read-only against the existing selector).
failureExamples: Adds @testing-library/react and @testing-library/dom to package.json devDependencies to write one EditorPane click test, blowing up the blast radius for a horizon that explicitly forbids it
Mutates the LastRun type in infrastructure/store.ts to add an 'isStale' flag, regressing Drawer.tsx:16 and DescPane which read the same type
Uses a TypeScript narrowing or default-value pattern that compiles under the dev tsconfig but trips strict mode in CI's tsc -b
Skips or .skip()s an existing sandbox test to 'keep vitest green' instead of fixing the underlying regression

phases.healerHint: Read the verdict via useAppStore.getState().lastRuns?.[currentSlug]?.verdict inside the Submit onClick — never from a closure or a component variable. Mirror the inline useState + two-stage button pattern from ManageProvidersModal.tsx:89 (local useState, no createPortal, no new component file, no overlay). Render 'Passed {passed} / {total}' in the block. Clear pendingSubmit in a useEffect on currentSlug AND in handleRun's finally, so the block closes on problem switches AND on every run completion.
